name_reason: Matches convention data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=animation, descriptor=ani_decoder_dst_buf accurately reflects the role (ANI frame decoder destination row-buffer base, a uint32 linear address). No Ghidra address residue in the name (no hex suffix equal to 0x52762). 'dst_buf' is a meaningful descriptor, not an address.
purpose: ANI.DAT frame decoder destination buffer base: the linear address of the destination row start that the row/sparse chunk handlers write decoded pixels into.
logic_summary: Part of the adjacent decoder-param trio (target_width @ 0x52760, dst_buf @ 0x52762, src_buf @ 0x52766). fd2_ani_decoder_set_target_buffer @ 0x36C8D stores the dst_buf argument here once per frame. Read by 6 chunk handlers: row handlers (fill_byte/copy_literal/decode_rle) write target_width bytes from offset 0 via memset/memcpy/RLE (REP STOSD); sparse handlers (set_byte/set_run_byte/copy_literal) treat it as base and index by offset (base[offset]). Palette chunk handlers use src_buf @ 0x52766 instead.
element_semantics: Single uint32 = 32-bit linear (flat) address of the destination row buffer start into which the current frame's decoded scanline pixels are written.
comment_original_issue: Original src comment's parenthetical '(REP STOSD/memcpy target)' was narrow: it omitted that the sparse chunk handlers use the value as an indexed base (base[offset]), not only a sequential memset/memcpy target, and did not note that palette handlers use src_buf instead.
notes: Memory at 0x52762 is 4 bytes of zero (BSS / zero-init, filled at runtime), consistent with a runtime-written pointer. Ghidra DATA type = uint len 4; primary symbol byte-identical to current name. Existing Ghidra PLATE_COMMENT is detailed and consistent with src understanding (lists all 6 readers + writer, palette-vs-row distinction, zero-init, adjacent trio) so it was left untouched per the 'only update plate if contradictory/stale/empty' rule. The older PRE_COMMENT is duplicative but not contradictory and was also left untouched (data plate canonically lives in PLATE_COMMENT). No logic changed; only the src comment block for this symbol was edited.
